stories.headline: Onsemi to buy Synaptics in ~$7B all-stock deal to expand into physical AI

key_facts.fact: ON Semiconductor (onsemi) agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock transaction with a total enterprise value of approximately $7 billion, its largest acquisition to date.
key_facts.excerpt: onsemi has agreed to acquire Synaptics in an all-stock transaction, representing a total enterprise value of approximately $7 billion.

key_facts.fact: Synaptics shareholders will receive a fixed 1.350 onsemi shares per Synaptics share, a roughly 19% premium to the two stocks' 10-day volume-weighted average prices, giving Synaptics holders about 12% of the combined company.
key_facts.excerpt: Synaptics shareholders will receive 1.35 shares of onsemi common stock for each Synaptics share, representing a roughly 19% premium... The transaction would give Synaptics shareholders about 12% ownership of the combined company on a fully diluted basis.

key_facts.fact: The combination is intended to position onsemi at the center of 'Physical AI,' with potential to expand its total addressable market by $30 billion to $243 billion by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: the potential to expand onsemi's TAM by $30 billion to $243 billion by 2030.

key_facts.fact: The deal, unanimously approved by both boards, is expected to close in mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal has been unanimously approved by both companies' boards and is expected to close in mid-2027, subject to Synaptics shareholder approval, regulatory clearances and customary closing conditions.

key_facts.fact: onsemi expects the acquisition to be accretive to adjusted earnings per share within 18 months of closing and to drive about $200 million in annual synergies; ON shares fell about 7.3% after hours to $110.12.
key_facts.excerpt: accretive to adjusted per-share earnings within 18 months of closing, adding that it will drive an expected $200 million in annual synergies... Shares of ON Semiconductor fell 7.3% to $110.12 after hours.

key_facts.fact: CEO Hassane El-Khoury said the deal adds Synaptics' Edge AI compute, human-machine interface and wireless connectivity to onsemi's power and sensing portfolio, targeting autonomous driving, robotics and AR/VR.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker also aims to capture growth from Synaptics' human-machine interface business and its broader technology and R&D in robotics and humanoid markets, El-Khoury said.

stories.headline: Apple raises Mac and iPad prices as AI memory shortage hits consumer tech

key_facts.fact: Apple raised prices across Macs, iPads, HomePods and Vision Pro on June 25, saying it could no longer shield customers from soaring memory and storage costs driven by the AI data-center buildout; the iPhone was left unchanged for now.
key_facts.excerpt: Amid a worldwide memory shortage driven by the AI buildout, Apple is raising prices of its Mac and iPad lineups... For the moment, there is no rise in iPhone prices.

key_facts.fact: Apple said in a statement: 'We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly. We have shielded our customers from these increases so far, but we have now reached a point where we need to begin raising prices.'
key_facts.excerpt: We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly. We have shielded our customers from these increases so far, but we have now reached a point where we need to begin raising prices on a number of products, including today's increases for iPad and Mac.

key_facts.fact: Specific increases included the MacBook Neo starting at $699 (up from $599), MacBook Air at $1,299 (up from $1,099), MacBook Pro with 1TB at $1,999 (up from $1,699), and the iPad Air 128GB at $749 (up from $599).
key_facts.excerpt: MacBook Neo now starts at $699 (up from $599), while MacBook Air now starts at $1299 (up from $1099). Other impacted products include MacBook Pro, iPad, iPad Air, and many more.

key_facts.fact: DRAM prices rose as much as 98% in Q1 2026 and are set to jump another 58% to 63% in the current quarter, per TrendForce, a surge dubbed 'RAMageddon'; memory makers like Micron have prioritized AI chipmakers such as Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Prices of dynamic random access memory... rose as much as 98 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 and are set to jump by another 58 per cent to 63 per cent in the current quarter, according to industry tracker TrendForce.

key_facts.fact: Data centers are expected to consume as much as 70% of total memory production in 2026, leaving phone and PC makers competing for the remainder.
key_facts.excerpt: By one widely cited estimate, data centres are expected to consume as much as 70% of total memory production in 2026... For every ten chips coming off a line, seven head to server farms.

stories.headline: US Commerce signs $250M CHIPS deal with Friedland's I-Pulse for silicon-carbide chips

key_facts.fact: The Department of Commerce's CHIPS Research & Development Office signed a definitive agreement with I-Pulse for a $250 million award under the CHIPS and Science Act to develop novel silicon-carbide (SiC) power semiconductors.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Commerce's CHIPS Research & Development Office today announced the signing of a definitive agreement with I-Pulse for a $250 million award under the CHIPS and Science Act.

key_facts.fact: I-Pulse, co-founded by mining billionaire Robert Friedland (CEO) and Laurent Frescaline (CTO), will develop high-temperature, high-current, high-voltage solid-state SiC switches for uses including underground mining, manufacturing, defense systems and geothermal drilling.
key_facts.excerpt: I-Pulse Co-founders Robert Friedland, CEO, and Laurent Frescaline, CTO, announced today a definitive agreement... commercialize cutting-edge, high-temperature, high-current, high-voltage solid-state switches. These switches have a multitude of applications including underground mining, rock crushing, manufacturing, and defense systems.

key_facts.fact: In connection with the award, the Department received a minority, non-controlling equity stake in I-Pulse.
key_facts.excerpt: In connection with the award, the Department received a minority, non-controlling equity stake in I-Pulse, which enhances the benefit to the U.S. taxpayer.

key_facts.fact: The program will be led by I-Pulse's Albuquerque, New Mexico team near Sandia National Laboratories and the Air Force Research Laboratory; the company also has facilities in Detroit and Toulouse, France.
key_facts.excerpt: The program would be led by the Albuquerque team, near Sandia National Laboratories and the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory, and would involve U.S. national laboratories, universities and specialized manufacturers.

key_facts.fact: Friedland said the funding will advance geothermal technology, arguing 'the limiting factor in artificial intelligence is clean energy... The best answer is geothermal'; I-Pulse investors include Rio Tinto and Newmont and it is 'likely to be a public company in a few years.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The limiting factor in artificial intelligence is clean energy, and you can't do AI with solar or wind. The best answer is geothermal.'... Closely held I-Pulse exceeded a $1 billion valuation a decade ago and is 'likely to be a public company in a few years,' Friedland said. Investors include large miners such as Rio Tinto Group and Newmont Corp.

stories.headline: Apple to skip high-end M6 chips, jump to AI-focused M7 line in 2027

key_facts.fact: Apple plans to release a base M6 chip as early as this year but has canceled the M6 Pro and M6 Max; the next Pro and Max chips will arrive in the M7 generation, marking the first Apple silicon line without a Pro or Max variant since 2020, per Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple plans to release an M6 chip for entry-level Macs as soon as this year, but it has canceled plans for higher-end M6 Pro and M6 Max chips. Instead, Apple's next Pro and Max chips will be part of its M7 chip lineup.

key_facts.fact: The base M7 is expected in the first half of 2027, with the M7 Pro and M7 Max at the end of 2027 and the M7 Ultra in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The base M7 chip is reportedly set for 'as early as the first half of next year.' The faster M7 Pro and M7 Max are slated for the end of next year, followed by the M7 Ultra in 2028.

key_facts.fact: The M7 line is designed primarily around major advancements to on-device AI processing, with the base M7 supporting about 240 GB/s of memory bandwidth, up from 153 GB/s on the M5.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The M7 line is designed primarily around major advancements to on-device AI processing,' Bloomberg reports. 'The base version is slated to support about 240 gigabytes per second of memory bandwidth.'

key_facts.fact: The base M6 (codenamed Komodo/H18G) is being tested in an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, with ~200 GB/s bandwidth and up to 12 GPU cores (vs 10 on the base M5).
key_facts.excerpt: The base M6 chip is reportedly being tested in an entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro. The chip is internally known as Komodo or H18G. It is expected to improve memory bandwidth to around 200 GB/s... Apple has reportedly tested configurations with up to 12 GPU cores, up from 10 cores on the base M5.

key_facts.fact: Apple still plans an M5 Ultra chip as early as this year for a new Mac Studio, with around 36 CPU cores and 80 GPU cores.
key_facts.excerpt: The company introduced the M5 Pro and Max chips earlier this year, and we expect to see the M6 announced for its entry-level MacBooks before the end of 2026.

stories.headline: Network automation startup Netris raises $15M Series A from a16z for AI neoclouds

key_facts.fact: Netris raised $15 million in a Series A round from Andreessen Horowitz; its software runs on network switches to help neocloud operators automate setup, configuration and operations and bring AI data centers online faster.
key_facts.excerpt: Netris has now raised $15 million in a Series A round from Andreessen Horowitz, TechCrunch has exclusively learned.

key_facts.fact: The platform is vendor-agnostic, compatible with both Nvidia and AMD servers, and isolates servers and resources at the hardware layer to enable multi-tenancy.
key_facts.excerpt: Saroyan said Netris' platform is vendor-agnostic, compatible with networking equipment and standards used at data centers, both for Nvidia and AMD's servers.

key_facts.fact: Netris is live at more than 35 GPU clusters worldwide, totaling about a million GPUs, operated by Lightning AI, Foxconn, Visionbay, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, TensorWave and Telus, among others.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Netris is live at more than 35 GPU clusters around the world (about a million GPUs total), operated by the likes of Lightning AI, Foxconn, Visionbay, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, TensorWave, Telus, and others.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia recommended Netris to several customers after being impressed by a demo of its technology two years ago.
key_facts.excerpt: Two years ago, the chipmaking giant was so impressed by a demo of Netris' technology that it recommended the company to several customers.

key_facts.fact: a16z partner Guido Appenzeller is joining Netris' board; the company will use the funding to hire engineers and sales staff and add support for more hardware vendors.
key_facts.excerpt: a16z partner Guido Appenzeller is joining the company's board. Looking forward, Netris aims to use the funding to hire more engineers and sales staff, add support for more hardware vendors.
